column1: # comment: "Lexicon alignments \u2014 OntoLex-Lemon, LIME, PROV-O, Wikidata. gmeow:LexicalItem and gmeow:LexicalForm are registry-independent, first-class information objects. The OntoLex alignment is by reference (Principle 5); GMEOW does not import OntoLex axioms. Reified constructs (UsageAttestation, EtymologicalDerivation) align to PROV-O at the entity/ derivation level; the full relator structure is available only in the canonical model. Frequency (FrAC), morphological (Morph), and lexicographic (Lexicog) projections are staged in the projection layer."

column6: An EtymologicalDerivation is a specialized provenance derivation with standpoint, confidence, and temporal scope. The full relator structure is lost in PROV-O projection.
GMEOW LexicalForm is broader than ontolex:Form (covers spoken, signed, reconstructed, and rendered forms, not just written).
GMEOW LexicalItem is broader than ontolex:LexicalEntry (covers morphemes, phrases, symbols, constructions, not just words), but the alignment is the closest surface term.
Wikidata 'lexeme' (Q181970) — a lexical item in a language, broader than a word.
A UsageAttestation is a provenance entity — information about observed use that can be attributed, derived, and versioned.

Structural difference: GMEOW models etymology via a reified EtymologicalDerivation relator (Derivation --etymonSource--> SourceItem), while PROV-O uses a direct binary property (DerivedItem --wasDerivedFrom--> SourceItem). Aligning etymonSource to prov:entity preserves the relator-level linkage to the source entity within the PROV-O Derivation structure, though the reified relator itself and its provenance metadata are lost in projection.
Lossy: ontolex:writtenRep covers only written forms; GMEOW formRepresentation also carries spoken (IPA), signed, reconstructed, and rendered forms.
Both link a lexical entity to its language. GMEOW uses a first-class gmeow:Language IRI; LIME expects a language tag string.
